item.title: Gaza Board of Peace says it will hand keys to UN if Israel fails to honour commitments
item.description:
Gaza Board of Peace says it will hand keys to UN if Israel fails to honour commitments

A senior adviser to the Trump-appointed Gaza Peace Council has warned that the body could return responsibility for the enclave to the United Nations if Israel does not honour its commitments under the 20-point plan, Israeli outlet Ynet has reported.

Josh Gruenbaum, who was appointed to the council by Trump and previously worked in the White House, told Ynet: “We have been extremely patient and have given Israel its space. But it is frustrating that now with the elections behind us — even if they haven’t resulted in a clear coalition — that Israel is failing to move forward on the commitments Netanyahu made to President Trump.” 

“If this political leadership says it no longer wants to honour what they committed to, just let us know,” Gruenbaum said “And we will throw the keys back to the UN.”

Ynet said it had seen a presentation prepared by council members, who visited Israel last week. Its final slide, titled “Other alternatives to Gaza”, reportedly lists several scenarios if the plan is abandoned.

These include a future US administration and Congress ordering a different reconstruction plan, the UN Security Council taking over “perhaps through UNRWA”, the Palestinian Authority and Hamas.

The last scenario, according to the slide, is that Israel becomes fully responsible for the administrative and humanitarian costs of Gaza’s population.

Another slide reportedly says Hamas formally accepted the plan in July, pledging to give up its weapons and transfer governmental powers to the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza (NCAG), the technocratic body meant to run the territory.

“We are at a standstill due to political elements within the Netanyahu government who have prevented us from progressing and from testing whether Hamas will keep its word,” Gruenbaum said, according to Ynet.

Israel has not acted on calls to protect Palestinian olive farmers, Ocha says
item.description:
Israel has not acted on calls to protect Palestinian olive farmers, Ocha says

Calls on the Israeli authorities to protect Palestinian olive farmers and ensure they can reach their groves safely have not been acted upon, the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (Ocha) said, citing the Humanitarian Country Team.

Instead, in the first nine months of 2026, Israeli authorities uprooted or otherwise damaged more than 10,000 Palestinian-owned trees and saplings across the West Bank, mostly olives, the statement adds.

The Humanitarian Country Team for the Occupied Palestinian Territory, which brings together UN bodies and humanitarian NGOs, said more than 400 Israeli settler attacks on the Palestinian olive harvest since September have resulted in casualties or damage to property, including to more than 4,000 trees and saplings.

The number of attacks this year exceeds that recorded in any previous olive harvest season. This year’s harvesting window is closing, the team said, but there is still some time to act.

"Humanitarian NGOs and UN agencies urge the Israeli authorities in the strongest possible terms: end all attacks on Palestinians and their livelihoods, as required by international law. Ensure farmers have free, safe, sufficient and reliable access to their land. The team added that perpetrators must be stopped and held to account," the statement read.

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said its aerospace forces have shot down a US MQ-9 drone over the Strait of Hormuz, state broadcaster Irib reported.

This was the 58th MQ-9 drone destroyed by Iranian forces, the report said.

item.title: UNDP official: 'Gaza's suffering must compel us to ask difficult questions'
item.description:
UNDP official: 'Gaza's suffering must compel us to ask difficult questions'

A top United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) official has said the suffering endured by people in Gaza "must compel us to ask difficult questions".

“What strikes you immediately is the scale of the destruction in Gaza, where more than 90% of the population depends on humanitarian assistance. The contrast between what we consider normal—food, water and quality of life—and the suffering endured by people in Gaza must compel us to ask difficult questions,” Haoliang Xu, Under-Secretary-General and Associate Administrator, UNDP, said.

Xu said a defining feature of our time is "polycrisis, with challenges that extend far beyond any one place", according to a post on X by MED Dialogues.

"The conflict in the Middle East, for example, is costing countries across the region at least 3.6% of GDP, with some UNDP estimates reaching 6%,” Xu said.

item.title: Trump warns Iran against reported ‘dirty bomb’ plot targeting Washington
item.description: US President Donald Trump on Friday threatened military action against Iran over reports of a possible “dirty bomb” plot targeting Washington, warning that his administration would not allow Tehran to pursue such a threat, Anadolu reports. Speaking to reporters at the White House, Trump was asked whether he had received additional intelligence about the alleged Iranian plot, whether the threat was credible and why Tehran might target the US capital. “There is a rumor that they are building a dirty bomb. If they do, we’re going to fight,” Trump said. item.title: Israeli attacks hit 4 districts in southern Lebanon, cause fires, damage
item.description: Israeli forces carried out attacks across four districts in southern Lebanon on Friday, causing fires and material damage, while Israeli drones continued flying over several areas, according to state media, Anadolu reports. Israeli aircraft launched two separate strikes on Kfar Tebnit in the Nabatieh district, coinciding with artillery shelling of Mansouri and Majdal Zoun, Lebanon’s state-run National News Agency (NNA) reported. In Nabatieh, Israeli artillery also targeted the area between Zawtar al-Sharqiya and Mayfadoun and the vicinity of the Ali al-Taher heights on the outskirts of Nabatieh al-Fawqa. The NNA said Israeli forces also started fires inside the Scout City on the eastern outskirts of Zawtar al-Sharqiya, with smoke seen rising from the area. item.description: Iran on Thursday pushed back against US allegations that Tehran is developing biological or chemical weapons, citing the US’ widely debunked claims before the 2000s Iraq War that Baghdad had weapons of mass destruction, Anadolu reports.
